findings.claim: Bracket validity is INVERSELY related to trend order across the set. The cleaner the moving-average stack, the less likely the engine found a stop it would accept.
findings.evidence: 9 of 18 names carry a textbook stack (ma20>ma50>ma100>ma200 with price above all four): BBY, GNW, CVX, MET, JNJ, UBS, SLDE, TAK, WELL. Six of those nine are BRACKET INVALID (CVX, MET, JNJ, UBS, SLDE, TAK) = 67% invalid. The other 9 names carry a disordered stack (an inversion, or price below an average): NFLX, CB, VRNS, DOCS, BSBR, MDT, SPGI, CTVA, GME. Seven of those nine are BRACKET VALID = 78% valid, only 22% invalid. Set totals reconcile: 10 valid / 8 invalid over 18. The mechanism is structural, not statistical: a trend that has run leaves no support close enough beneath price to satisfy the rr>=2.0 and risk%-ceiling gates, while a damaged chart has overhead supply directly above price that the engine converts into a target ladder.

findings.claim: The three names trading BELOW their own 200-day average all have valid brackets, and they produced three of the four highest reward ratios in the set. High rr here is a symptom of broken structure, not of opportunity.

Ranking all ten valid brackets by rr: DOCS 7.01, GME 4.99, CB 4.37, NFLX 3.37, BSBR 2.75... — three of the top four are the three sub-200-day names. Their 'targets' are the undersides of the broken averages stacked above price.

findings.claim: 'BRACKET VALID' is not a uniform quality stamp: four of the ten valid brackets pass their gate only at TP2, with a first target paying less than 1R.
findings.evidence: rr_tp1 below 1.0 on BSBR 0.05, WELL 0.28, MDT 0.48, BBY 0.74 — four of ten. Their headline rr values (2.75, 2.02, 2.01, 2.37) are all TP2 numbers. Meanwhile the valid brackets that genuinely pay at TP1 are CB 2.83, NFLX 2.47, GME 4.46, DOCS 4.92, GNW 1.29, VRNS 1.07 — and three of those six (NFLX, GME, DOCS) are the broken-structure names from finding 2. findings.claim: The ATR fallback stop makes the eight bracketless names look CHEAPER on risk than the names with real structural stops. That is backwards and it is a live sizing hazard.
findings.evidence: atr_fallback_stop as a percentage of price for the 8 invalid names: TAK 1.55%, UBS 1.63%, CVX 1.85%, MET 1.90%, JNJ 2.03%, SPGI 2.65%, CTVA 2.65%, SLDE 2.95%. Every one of those is tighter than four of the ten real structural risks — DOCS 9.67%, VRNS 6.11%, BBY 4.27%, NFLX 4.32% — and six of the eight are tighter than MDT's 3.62% ma200 stop and BSBR's 3.32%. But by definition the fallback is exactly 1x atr_14d below price: one ordinary day's range, on a line nothing has defended. TAK's 0.29 and UBS's 0.91 will be taken out by noise. Worst case: SPGI's fallback 438.63 sits BELOW its ma200 446.85, so the arithmetic stop only fires after the trend read has already failed — the one name in the set where the fallback is beneath the level that defines the thesis.

findings.evidence: 32 seat-nominations across 18 names. BBY took the most (4 seats, conviction sum 12) on structure 50.5 — second-lowest in the set — with shift RANGE and, on my own machinery, lens_positive 0 (leadership ok, coil ok, insti_money ok, structure ok, resistance warn, sector ok: not one strong). By contrast the five highest structure readings — CTVA 91.6, CVX 83.2, SLDE 82.1, BSBR 81.1, SPGI 81.1 — drew 1, 2, 1, 1 and 1 seat respectively: 6 seats over 5 names, 1.2 per name. The five lowest structure readings among nominated names — GME 31.6, CB 44.2, BBY 50.5, WELL 60.0, GNW 68.4 — drew 1, 2, 4, 2 and 3: 12 seats over 5 names, 2.4 per name, exactly double. Cross-cut by my grades: the 5 CLEAN names averaged 2.2 seats, the 10 MIXED 1.6, the 3 BROKEN 1.7.

findings.claim: Lens confirmation and bracket validity point in opposite directions, which is the same inversion as finding 1 arriving on an independent axis.
findings.evidence: Six names read lens_positive 4 (the maximum in this set): GNW, CVX, MET, JNJ, BSBR, TAK. Four of those six are BRACKET INVALID — CVX, MET, JNJ, TAK. The two lens-strongest names with valid brackets are GNW (risk 2.31%, rr_tp1 1.29) and BSBR (rr_tp1 0.05). At the other end, the three names I grade BROKEN read lens_positive 2 (NFLX), 3 (DOCS) and 1 with 3 warnings (GME) — and all three are bracket-valid. Lens confirmation is computed from leadership/coil/insti_money/structure/resistance/sector and shares no input with the bracket gates, so this is corroboration rather than restatement.

findings.claim: Not one of the eighteen names sits in an advancing sector. The entire deliberation set was nominated against a sector tape AQE labels fading, recovering or declining.
findings.evidence: sector_trend_state across the set: 'Momentum Fading — Hold, Don't Add' on 14 names (GNW, NFLX, CB, CVX, VRNS, MET, JNJ, UBS, DOCS, SLDE, BSBR, MDT, SPGI, TAK); 'Recovering From Weakness — Watch for Entry' on 3 (BBY, WELL, GME); 'Declining — Avoid' on 1 (CTVA). Zero advancing. With no Layer 0 filter today and the full 164-name universe available, 50 names drew a nomination and the 18 that qualified contain no name whose sector is being read as advancing.

My card states plainly that '--' means no data and absence is never agreement — these two names have the thinnest confirmation in the set and the highest ranks.

declarations: canon_status: HAND-TRANSCRIBED, UNGROUNDED — no canon.lock.yaml, no sealed extract, citations not re-verifiable (see PROVENANCE on my card). This filing carries less weight at the desk than a grounded voice's and the PM should read it that way.
tape_read: NOT_APPLICABLE (premarket). No Level 2, print rate or live spread exists before the open and I have not inferred tape state from bars (C6-C11).
spread_read: NOT_APPLICABLE (premarket), same basis as tape_read (C10).

ranking_formula: sc_momentum is used as the set's ranking spine and it is NOT Clenow's regression-slope x R-squared (C12). Different construct, never conflated. The rank field I cite (e.g. SLDE rank 6, CTVA rank 8) is AQE's, not a momentum-slope rank.
gap_filter: NOT_SERVED (C15). day_vol and atr_14d are dispersion measures, not single-day gap-event flags, so nothing here reads gap risk.
trend_filter: SERVED — ma_50 / ma_100 / ma_200 are real fields and every trend-order grade in this filing rests on them (C1, C14, C15).

N=18 is a set of names, not a sample. The bracket-validity-versus-trend-order inversion in finding 1 (6/9 versus 2/9) is a description of today's deliberation set and a statement about the bracket engine's gate mechanics. It is not a backtested edge and I have not tested it across days.

Whole-chart, multi-week phase judgment is out of my scope and belongs to the wyckoff seat. Every read above is a single-bar or fixed-sequence mechanical test on printed fields — trend order, shift state, lens labels, ATR distance, participation ratio.
MIXED is not a hedge. Every MIXED grade names the specific field that is clean and the specific field that is not; where the two halves disagree (SLDE, CTVA) the disagreement is the finding.
